data.title: Oman's Muscat Municipality expected to award stormwater drain works contract in Q4 2026
data.description:
By Staff Writer

Oman's Muscat Municipality is evaluating bids for a design-and-build contract to develop and rehabilitate stormwater drainage infrastructure at multiple locations in Wilayat Seeb, Muscat Governorate.

The tender for the Wilayat Seeb Surface Stormwater Drainage Network project was issued on 13 September 2026, with bids due on 8 October 2026.

“The contract is expected to be awarded in December 2026,” a source aware of the details told Zawya Projects, adding that project completion targeted for the fourth quarter of 2028.

According to project information, five contractors are listed as bidders: Rukn Construction Engineering and Electromechanical, Ruwaished International Establishment, Crystal Glory Contracting, Gulf National Ways, and Awfait Trading and Contracting Establishment.

The scope includes wadi alignment works, drainage channel improvements, rehabilitation of stormwater flow paths and erosion and scour protection at various locations across Wilayat Seeb.

Construction activities will include adjustments to wadi beds, channel rehabilitation, installation of riprap and mortared riprap protection, drainage-related works and associated civil infrastructure.

(Reporting by Deva Palanisamy; Editing by Anoop Menon)

data.title: AI is forcing recruitment firms to overhaul their business models
data.description:
New Delhi, Oct. 31 -- Recruitment companies are changing the way they work as artificial intelligence (AI) tools take over functions such as resume sourcing, background checks, skillset matching, and even conduct the first couple of rounds of candidate interviews.

The result? Staffing firms-typically into temporary hiring-are moving towards mandates that need candidates with complex skillsets and more years of work experience. To retain clients, some have created their own hiring tools to offer faster services to larger groups of clients, while others are outsourcing the initial phase of their hiring to AI platforms.

However, there is gnawing worry that clients will ask for a drop in billing rates as companies realize that candidate sourcing may not require as many hiring agents.

Take the case of Quess Corp. Ltd, one of the top three staffing firms in India, which has rebranded its key IT staffing vertical to IT Solutions to offer more than just plain vanilla recruitment. The company said demand for candidates with at least four years of experience has been rising.

"Our data for January-September this year, compared with the same period last year, shows that demand for professionals with 0-4 years of experience declined by 22%, while demand for those with 4-10 years increased by 14%, and for those with over 10 years rose by 40%," said Kapil Joshi, chief executive officer of Quess IT Solutions.

The recruitment sector is largely split into four broad categories of firms - those that are into gig hiring, typically in the delivery space, where one person can be employed by many companies; staffing firms; those that look only into permanent roles for clients, and executive search companies that hire CXOs. The demarcations are not stringent and many hiring firms work across these services to cater to a larger client base.

AI's impact is felt largely by those in mass recruitment because the skillset matching is basic and there may be only 2-3 interview rounds. If skillset matching, resume sourcing, interview scheduling and even the first round of candidate testing is done by AI, that leaves very little work for the HR firm.

Headhunters responsible for CXO hiring so far remain less impacted by AI because the sourcing and hiring process takes months, depending on the equation and comfort between the candidate, the headhunter and the client company. Interviews can often go 7-8 rounds as multiple stakeholders gauge the candidate.

Some startups have cropped up to take care of the entire hiring cycle with AI recruitment tools-understanding demand, sourcing resumes, stack ranking, automated candidate reach-outs and conducting contextual AI interviews in real time. Bengaluru-based RazorSwift is one of them.

"Today, about 60% of a recruiter's tasks are administrative and this time can be used to scale services that involve more interaction with the candidate," said Aravind Sridharan, founder and CEO of RazorSwift.

The startup charges clients Rs.75,000 to Rs.3 lakh a month, depending on the size and scale of the enterprise.

"AI-driven interviews range between Rs.500-650 for a 30-minute interview and Rs.1,000 for an hour-long interview," Sridharan said.

In the six months since the commercial launch of the products, the startup has roped in six companies, including recruitment firms, that have given them the entire hiring stack.

However, not all acknowledge the swiftness in turnaround time. Kamal Karanth, co-founder of recruitment firm Xpheno, said the scale and speed at the recruiter's end may have gone up but the client still takes time to decide on candidates and the hiring cycle has not changed.

The other concern is billing clients. According to CIEL HR Services, recruitment firms may be forced to reconsider their billing rates in a few months.

"At every step of the hiring process, AI has entered and this will impact billing models. Pricing is a reflection of the value one delivers and if AI takes up a major chunk of the work, then the billing models will change based on the value delivered," said Aditya Narayan Mishra, managing director and CEO of CIEL HR.

Recruitment firms have various billing formats. In some cases, it could be a flat fee structure, especially in case of volumes. In others, it could be a percentage of the cost to the company, depending on the seniority and complexity of the role.

Karanth said billing rates will not change because AI tools-even if built in-house-have a cost.

"Xpheno uses its own AI tool called Vector to source and shortlist candidates and developing it was expensive. Therefore, the billing rate remains around 12.5% because the cost of AI is built in," said the co-founder.

However, the number of recruiters needed for a project has dropped.

"Earlier, I needed 10 recruiters to service two clients. Now, I need the same number to work with five clients."

data.title: The week in charts: Anthropic's IPO, falling air traffic and Ather's return to profit
data.description:
New Delhi, Oct. 31 -- From Anthropic PBC preparing for its initial public offering (IPO) to domestic air passenger traffic posting its steepest September decline since the covid-19 pandemic, Ather Energy Ltd turning profitable, domestic workers worldwide earning less relative to other employees, and Harry Kane becoming the first English player since 2001 to win the men's Ballon d'Or, here are this week's news in numbers.

Five-year-old generative artificial intelligence company Anthropic publicly filed for an IPO in the US, providing new financial details on the scale, scope, and challenges of its ambitious operation.

In the June quarter, Anthropic posted revenues of $11.55 billion, up from $4.73 billion in the March quarter. The company behind the Claude models also posted its maiden operating profit, of $974 million. Its operating loss for the six months stood at $693 million.

Some current and prospective investors are valuing Anthropic at about $1.5 trillion, down from roughly $2 trillion earlier in October. The lower estimate still represents an increase of more than 50% from the $965 billion valuation at its May funding round.

Domestic air passenger traffic fell for the fourth straight month in September. Passenger numbers stood at 11.82 million, down from 12.64 million a year ago. This was the steepest year-on-year decline since the pandemic.

September is traditionally a lean month for airlines, but weaker demand has coincided with higher airfares and capacity cuts as carriers grapple with rising fuel costs linked to the West Asia war.

In Delhi, aviation turbine fuel (ATF) prices rose nearly 25% in three months, from about Rs.110 a litre in July to Rs.137 on 1 October. The increase is adding to airlines' costs, with carriers raising fuel surcharges and reducing capacity.

Electric two-wheeler manufacturer Ather Energy reported its maiden quarterly net profit in the September quarter. Amid a brisk pick-up in electric vehicle sales, its operating revenue rose 63% year-on-year to Rs.1,464 crore, while net profit stood at Rs.1.26 crore.

In the last 10 quarters, Ather has crafted a consistent drive towards profitability. The company's earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization (Ebitda) margin improved from a loss of 35.6% in Q1 of FY25 to a positive margin of 0.8% in Q2 of FY27.

Even as Ather's production grew 45% to 98,400 units, the management said monthly retail demand of 18,000-20,000 units remained unmet due to supply constraints.

21%: The premium over the issue price at which Jio Platforms Ltd's shares listed on the stock exchanges, giving the telecom major a market capitalization of about Rs.12.5 trillion, second only to parent Reliance Industries Ltd.

6.7%: Year-on-year growth in India's industrial production in September, down from a revised 7.8% in August. Manufacturing and electricity output growth moderated, while mining activity contracted further.

$27 billion: The amount raised by global private equity firm Advent International for its 11th flagship fund, exceeding its $26 billion target. It also raised more than $3 billion for its new mid-market strategy.

$20 million: The amount provisionally allocated to Nepal by the UN's Fund for responding to loss and damage following the devastating August floods. The allocation is less than 1% of the estimated reconstruction cost.

35: The number of balls India's Abhishek Sharma took to score a century against New Zealand in the third T20 international, setting a record for the fastest T20I century against the Black Caps.

Domestic workers worldwide earned an average of just 53.3% of the average monthly wage of other employees across all other sectors in 2025, down from 56.4% in 2019.

According to a statistical brief released by the International Labour Organization (ILO) on 27 October, this points to a widening relative wage gap. While the brief did not release country-level data, it provided estimates by income group. Domestic workers earned 53.7% of other employees' average monthly wages in high-income countries, 56.6% in middle-income countries and 36% in low-income countries.

The study estimates that 80 million people aged 15 and above were employed as domestic workers worldwide in 2025, including cleaners, helpers, drivers and cooks. About 83% of them were informally employed, without effective labour and social protection.

Bayern Munich striker Harry Kane became the first English player to win the men's Ballon d'Or-football's top individual prize-since Michael Owen in 2001.

He is the fifth Englishman to win the award, though English players have won it six times, with Kevin Keegan claiming it twice. The other winners were Bobby Charlton and Stanley Matthews. Argentina and France are tied with eight wins each.

Kane beat France's Kylian Mbappe and Spain's Lamine Yamal to the award. Kane scored 73 goals in 65 matches during the 2025-26 season, including 61 for Bayern Munich.

Among individual players, Lionel Messi of Argentina has won it the most times (eight), followed by Cristiano Ronaldo of Portugal (five). Spain's Alexia Putellas won the women's Ballon d'Or for the third time in her career this year.

data.title: Why Swiggy's Toing is raising questions over food-delivery profitability
data.description:
Bengaluru, Oct. 31 -- Swiggy Ltd's affordable-meal app Toing has prompted questions from analysts about whether the food-delivery company can expand its customer base without diluting the profitability of its core business.

"Food delivery is a tricky business because competition is intense and customers are sensitive to pricing. The question for Swiggy is whether Toing can bring in incremental demand without putting further pressure on the economics of its core platform," said Satish Meena, analyst at Datum Intelligence.

Launched to attract price-sensitive consumers, Toing gives the company another way to reach customers who may be unwilling to pay for meals through its main app. In its latest shareholder letter, it said the offering could help lift growth in its combined food-delivery marketplace to 25-30%, compared with its guidance of 18-20% for the core business, excluding Toing.

However, brokerages beg to differ. In a note dated 23 October, JM Financial said it saw "zero rationale" for operating Toing as a separate business, arguing that it uses the same restaurant and delivery-partner networks as Swiggy's core platform and serves an overlapping customer base.

The brokerage also raised concerns about cannibalization, cash burn and the incremental value created by the offering. It recommended discontinuing Toing and redirecting resources towards the core food-delivery business.

Swiggy's Platform Innovations segment, which includes experimental initiatives such as Toing, reported an adjusted earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization (Ebitda) loss of Rs.162 crore in the September quarter, up from Rs.131 crore in the June quarter. The company does not disclose Toing's standalone financials.

The company, meanwhile, has pointed to early signs that Toing is attracting new or returning users. Two out of every three Toing users were either first-time Swiggy users or customers who had been inactive for an extended period.

Customers ordering through both apps also had a combined order frequency about 25% higher than their individual order frequency on either platform, it said. These figures suggest Toing could help increase engagement, although they do not establish how much of the growth is incremental to the overall marketplace.

The company also acknowledged that demand had shifted between Toing and its main app in ways that were difficult to predict. "There was some interplay of demand levers on one platform versus the other, which was hard to predict as we built out both the offerings," Swiggy said in its September quarter shareholder letter.

It said it was seeing "early green shoots of business-market fit", with unit economics turning positive among repeat users in the cities where Toing was launched first. However, it said monetization and cost structures still needed to improve, with greater clarity on the model's scalability expected over the next one to two quarters.

The questions around Toing come as Swiggy faces a broader execution challenge against Eternal Ltd, which operates Zomato, across food delivery and quick commerce. CLSA highlighted a gap between the two companies in growth and profitability in the second quarter of fiscal year 2026-27 (FY27), noting that sustained operational improvements would be needed to rebuild investor confidence.

Competition in food delivery is also intensifying, with new entrants such as Flipkart and Shiprocket increasing investments to acquire customers and encourage more frequent ordering.

Eternal chief financial officer Akshant Goyal said during the company's Q2 earnings call that competitive intensity was higher in the September quarter than in the preceding few quarters, partly driven by Eternal's own investments.

"We've been aggressively investing in growth," Goyal said. Investments in acquiring new customers and increasing order frequency among existing users had risen over the past few quarters, he said, adding that the trend was likely to continue.

Eternal's food-delivery business reported net order value (NOV) of Rs.11,445 crore in the quarter, up 21.5% year-on-year. Adjusted Ebitda rose 25% to Rs.627 crore, equivalent to 5.5% of NOV.

Swiggy, meanwhile, reported food-delivery gross order value (GOV) growth of 17.7% to Rs.10,054 crore. Adjusted Ebitda rose to Rs.341 crore from Rs.240 crore a year ago. It said its core food-delivery business, excluding Toing, grew more than 20% on-year and reiterated its full-year growth guidance of 18-20%.

Toing's longer-term prospects will depend on whether the app can attract customers and increase order frequency without simply shifting transactions away from its main platform, according to Datum Intelligence's Meena.

"New initiatives in food and internet businesses can take time to find their footing, but companies must also be prepared to discontinue experiments that fail to demonstrate a viable business model," he noted.

Despite the concerns around Toing, brokerage Nomura said food delivery remained a "cash cow" for Swiggy and expected the business to generate Rs.1,300-1,900 crore in Ebitda in FY27 and FY28. It retained a buy rating on the stock while cutting its target price to Rs.300. Swiggy's shares were down 4.8% at Rs.176.60 apiece on Friday at 3pm, even as the Sensex rose 0.49%.

data.title: China's factory activity marks third contraction in four months
data.description:
Key points:
  • Official manufacturing PMI falls to 49.3 in October from 50.1 in September
  • Non-manufacturing PMI falls to 49.7 from 50.2 in September
  • New orders and new export orders stay in contraction territory in October

China's factory activity unexpectedly dropped in October, its third contraction in four months, a government survey showed on Saturday, hurt by soft demand for exports as well as goods at home.

The official manufacturing purchasing managers' index (PMI) fell to 49.3 from 50.1 in September, according to data from the National Bureau of Statistics. That missed a forecast for 50.0 from a Reuters poll.

Factory activity weakened as overseas Christmas-related orders, which were front-loaded in September, cooled in October. It was also hurt when consumer spending, which climbed during China's long National Day holiday in the first week of October, fizzled out after, in a return to its long-stagnant state.

"Insufficient demand is increasing downward pressure on the economy," said Zhang Liqun, an analyst with the China Federation of Logistics & Purchasing, adding that policymakers should take the problem seriously and step up measures as soon as possible.

Sub-indexes for new orders overall and for new export orders both stayed in contraction territory in October. Production and purchasing activity also slipped into contraction from expansion.

The non-manufacturing PMI, which covers services and construction, also dropped, to 49.7 from 50.2 in September.

The readings are compiled based on purchasing managers' reports about whether conditions improved, worsened or were unchanged in areas such as new orders, output and employment compared with the previous month. A reading above 50 signals expansion, while one below 50 indicates contraction.

Some sectors within manufacturing were doing well.

Production and new orders sub-indexes for railway, shipbuilding, aerospace equipment, and computer, communications and electronics manufacturing were all at or above 53.0, the survey showed.

AI-related firms in particular have reported strong earnings growth. Zhongji Innolight , a maker of high-speed optical modules that connect servers and switches in AI data centres, posted a near tripling in third-quarter net profit.

But the lacklustre domestic market and rising costs have weighed on many old-school manufacturers and property-linked firms. Custom furniture maker Oppein Home , for example, saw net profit plunge 80% during the quarter.

China's economy is, however, expected to meet the country's 4.5-5.0% annual growth target without additional stimulus measures after third-quarter growth rebounded to 4.5% from 4.3% in April-June.

data.title: Qatar's Ashgal likely to award air base infrastructure works contract in Q1 2027
data.description:
By Staff Writer

Qatar's Public Works Authority (Ashghal) is likely to award construction tender for road and infrastructure works surrounding Al Udeid Air Base in the first quarter of 2027, a source aware of the details said.

The tender, issued on 22 October, covers the construction of a dual-carriageway access road, three roundabouts and associated infrastructure within an approved 40-metre-wide right-of-way corridor.

The bids submission deadline is 22 November 2026.

“The construction contract is expected to be awarded in March 2027, with completion targeted for the third quarter of 2028,” the source told Zawya Projects.

The proposed road will connect to the existing CD road of Al Majd Road on the eastern side and Street 203 in Zone 95 on the western side, improving access to Al Udeid Air Base.

The infrastructure scope includes road construction, street lighting, intelligent transport systems (ITS), directional signage and a surface water drainage network.

data.title: Irdai's proposed insurance commission caps may hit smaller banks harder
data.description:
MUMBAI, Oct. 31 -- Banks are preparing for a sharp hit to fee income from proposed caps on insurance distribution commissions, with smaller and mid-sized lenders facing a disproportionately higher impact than their larger peers.

The proposed curbs could erode more than half the bancassurance income at some small and mid-sized lenders, with losses reaching as much as 70% in certain product categories. Several lenders, including small finance banks (SFBs), flagged the potential hit while reporting their second-quarter earnings, as they assessed the impact of the Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India's (Irdai) proposals.

Irdai's 23 September consultation paper proposed product-wise limits on commissions paid by insurers to banks, brokers and agents. It also seeks to bar lenders from making insurance purchases compulsory alongside loans.

Single-premium life insurance policies sold alongside loans, a key source of fee income for many lenders, would carry a commission cap of 2%. Currently, there is no fixed commission cap for these policies, with banks earning commissions based on bilateral agreements with insurers. For credit-life products, commissions can currently go as high as 45%, according to industry estimates.

"Private banks have higher exposure to insurance distribution income, with its contribution to profitability increasing steadily. Thus, these banks are likely to be more sensitive to the proposed reduction in commissions for open-architecture insurance distribution entities (IDEs) and credit-linked insurance," ratings agency Icra said in a note earlier this month. Lower commissions could "moderately affect" banks' fee income, it added.

The impact is expected to be more pronounced among private banks, particularly mid-sized and smaller lenders, for whom insurance distribution comprises a much higher share of other income. Larger banks, however, are better placed to absorb some of the losses. At ICICI Bank's post-results press conference, executive director Sandeep Batra said bancassurance fees account for less than 1% of the bank's total income, making the impact on profits minimal.

Bandhan Bank expects its third-party income to decline by around Rs.200 crore annually, its management said during the bank's second-quarter media call. RBL Bank executive director Jaideep Iyer said on the lender's earnings call that a 50-60% reduction in its annual bancassurance income of roughly Rs.300 crore "should be minimum to be penciled in". Karur Vysya Bank said commissions on some life insurance products could fall by as much as 70%.

Union Bank of India managing director and chief executive Asheesh Pandey said in a media call that insurance and other commission income currently accounts for about 8% of the bank's total fee income. The lender could see a hit of Rs.100-110 crore if the proposed norms are implemented.

Even larger banks, particularly those with group insurance companies, are concerned about the impact on business economics. HDFC Bank chief financial officer Srinivasan Vaidyanathan said on the post-earnings call that the proposed reduction in commission rates was "quite high" and could have a "pretty high impact".

Insurance income accounted for 7.3% of HDFC Bank's profit before tax in FY26, compared with just 0.6% at ICICI Bank. Among smaller lenders, the share was highest at 30.8% for Bandhan Bank, followed by 19.2% for Ujjivan SFB and 14.3% for AU SFB, according to a JM Financial report.

Ujjivan SFB's Hitendra Jha, who heads retail liabilities and third-party products, said roughly half the lender's insurance income came from credit-linked policies, the category facing the steepest cuts. This income "largely flows to our bottom line", he said.

The potential impact also appears higher than the initial estimates made by analysts when Irdai issued its consultation paper on 23 September.

Saurabh Bhalerao, director - BFSI at CareEdge Ratings, said the absolute numbers did not fully capture the extent of the impact on some lenders.

"From a topline perspective, it is not a big hit. But, if you look at insurance income as a share of net profit, that's where you see how dependent these banks are, and for smaller banks it's a much more substantial hit," he said.

To cushion the impact, banks are looking to deepen insurance penetration, sell more policies and improve their product mix. Some are also looking to expand other fee-generating businesses, such as mutual fund distribution, forex, credit cards and trade finance. The strategy will be to make up for lower commissions through higher volumes, even as lenders assess how much of the lost income can realistically be recovered.

Bandhan Bank plans to expand its insurance business in tier 2, 3 and 4 towns, where commission rates are higher, while also growing its mutual fund distribution business. Karur Vysya Bank estimates it could recover the lost income by increasing life insurance penetration from about 1.6% currently to 3.8-3.9%.

HDFC Bank expects lower-priced policies to attract more customers and improve persistency, while AU SFB plans to focus on other fee-generating businesses, including forex, credit cards and trade finance.

data.title: Egypt's Uptown 6 October signs deal for $108mln outlet mall project
data.description:
By Marwa Abo Almajd

Egyptian developer Uptown 6 October for Development and Investment has signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) with UK-based Fashion House Group (FHG) to support the development and operation of an international outlet shopping destination within its planned Grand Uptown Mall (GUM) project in New October City.

The mixed-use retail and leisure development is expected to involve investments exceeding 6 billion Egyptian pounds ($108 million approximately) and have a total leasable area of around 90,000 square metres (sqm), according to the preliminary master plan.

The first phase is scheduled to open in October 2028, subject to the completion of designs, technical studies, construction and regulatory approvals, the developer said in a statement.

Under the MoU, Fashion House Group will provide expertise in outlet centre development and operations, including leasing strategies, international brand acquisition, tenant mix management, marketing and operational planning.

Emtelak Real Estate Investment Fund is participating as a strategic investment partner in the project.

The development will include Fashion House International Outlet, GUM Luxury House and Fashion House Street, alongside a boutique hotel, restaurants, cafés, entertainment facilities and business spaces.

Other planned components include a VIP theatre, family entertainment centre, business club and a gallery showcasing Egyptian handicrafts.

The project will also incorporate an e-commerce platform offering delivery and click-and-collect services.

Ahmed Abouzaid, Chairman of Uptown 6 October Group, said the development was intended to combine retail, hospitality and entertainment facilities and support commercial activity in New October City.

Brendon O'Reilly, Managing Director of Fashion House Group and Fashion House Outlet Centres, said the company would draw on its European outlet retail experience and relationships with international brands to support the project.

Fashion House Group has more than 25 years of experience in outlet centre development and operations, with projects in Romania, Poland and Russia.

Separately, Uptown 6 October Education signed an agreement with GSM Holding to establish GSM Egypt, a company focused on developing and operating educational institutions.

The developer also announced an extension of its British International School agreement from 15 to 25 years.

In the investment sector, Uptown 6 October announced an agreement with Alpha Financial Investment Management to manage the Emtelak Real Estate Investment Fund and prepare an initial subscription prospectus.

The group also signed an agreement with ROX to establish RAQAM Real World Assets, a venture focused on block chain-based real estate tokenisation and digital registration, subject to applicable regulations.

(1 US Dollar = 55.74 Egyptian pounds)

(Writing by Marwa Abo Almajd; Editing by Anoop Menon)

data.title: Stocktwits Defense Watch: L3Harris, BA Report Record Backlogs, HII Raises FY2026 Shipbuilding Revenue Forecast
data.description:
Key points:
  • L3Harris reported a record $53.2 billion backlog after securing $19.3 billion in quarterly orders.
  • HII secured $32.4 billion in new contracts during Q3, with existing awards covering nearly 90% of its expected shipbuilding revenue through 2030.
  • Boeing’s defense revenue jumped 15% to $7.94 billion, but weaker commercial airplane performance weighed on overall results.

With the quarterly earnings season in full swing, U.S. defense firms largely delivered strong results this week, highlighting sharp growth in backlogs driven by rising demand for missiles, military aircraft and naval vessels.

L3Harris Technologies (LHX), Boeing (BA), and HII (HII) all reported topline growth, and while Boeing’s earnings fell short of street expectations, the aircraft maker attributed it to weaker performance of its commercial airplanes division.

L3Harris Raises Outlook As Backlog Hits Record $53.2B

On Thursday, L3Harris reported a 7% increase in third-quarter (Q3) revenue to $6.06 billion, beating Wall Street estimates of $5.94 billion, according to Fiscal.ai. Earnings per share (EPS) jumped 33% to $3.28, beating consensus estimates of $2.95.

Crucially, L3Harris reported a record backlog of $53.2 billion, boosted by quarterly orders of around $19.3 billion. CEO Sam Mehta highlighted strong demand for missile systems, space technologies and military communications equipment.

The outperformance allowed the company to raise its full-year 2026 revenue outlook to $23.5 billion to $23.7 billion from $23.2 billion to $23.7 billion and EPS guidance to $12.25 to $12.35 from $11.80 to $12.00.

LHX shares closed 6.8% higher on Thursday.

HII Secures $32.4B In New Orders In Q3

On Thursday, another defense contractor posted a strong quarterly print. Shipbuilder HII reported record third-quarter revenue of $3.54 billion, up nearly 11% and above Wall Street’s $3.37 billion estimates. EPS surged around 49% to $5.48, significantly higher than the $4.43 estimates.

New contract awards during the quarter totaled $32.4 billion, accounting for the majority of the $43.1 billion in contracts it received year-to-date.

CEO Chris Kastner added that existing awards now cover about 90% of expected shipbuilding revenue through 2030. HII raised its 2026 shipbuilding revenue forecast to $10.5 billion to $10.7 billion from $10.2 billion to $10.4 billion.

HII shares surged after the results, closing 13.2% higher.

Boeing’s Defense Business Grows But Q3 Earnings Miss Street Estimates

Boeing’s 4% topline growth primarily reflected higher defense and services volume. The company’s defense division recorded a 15% increase in Q3 revenue to $7.94 billion.

While earnings from operations and operating margins grew significantly over the last year, the gains reflected a $252 million gain from the sale of HRL Laboratories in July. The division’s backlog reached a record $101 billion.

Overall, revenue came in at $24.19 billion, along with a loss of $0.34 per share. Both metrics were below Street estimates. Revenue from its largest segment, commercial airplanes, declined 3%.

BA shares tanked nearly 11% after the results on Tuesday.

How Have LHX, HII And BA Stocks Performed In 2026?

Retail sentiment surrounding LHX and HII on Stocktwits turned ‘neutral’ from ‘bearish’ over the past 24 hours. Sentiment for BA remained in the ‘bullish’ territory.

Despite strong earnings-driven rallies in L3Harris and HII, all three stocks remain in negative territory year-to-date, with Boeing down nearly 21%, HII falling 9.6%, and L3Harris declining 8.6%.

data.title: EBRD arranges $265mln financing for ADD Properties' Egypt hospitality expansion
data.description:
By Marwa Abo Almajd

The European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) is arranging a $265 million financing package to support the expansion and modernisation of ADD Properties' hospitality portfolio in Egypt, including the development of a new Grand Hyatt hotel in West Cairo.

ADD Properties, a member of Sami Saad Holding, will use the financing to strengthen its capital structure, support investment in its hospitality assets and enhance the value of its portfolio, according to EBRD’s press statement.

The EBRD is acting as initial mandated lead arranger and bookrunner, providing the largest loan facility of $127.5 million.

The International Finance Corporation (IFC) is providing $60 million as a mandated lead arranger under the Mutual Reliance Framework.

Emirates NBD Egypt is contributing $40 million and will act as a mandated lead arranger, global facility agent and onshore account bank.

The National Bank of Egypt is providing $37.5 million and will serve as a mandated lead arranger, local facility agent, onshore security agent and onshore account bank.

DenizBank, a subsidiary of Emirates NBD Group, is acting as offshore security agent and offshore account bank.

EFG Hermes, part of EFG Holding, is serving as sole financial adviser and bookrunner for the transaction.

The financing will support ADD Properties' (formerly known as ALDAU Development) hospitality investment programme, anchored by the planned Grand Hyatt development in West Cairo.

The package will also be complemented by technical assistance to support the company's environmental and corporate governance initiatives.

These include the development of a high-performance hotel, certification of existing hospitality assets to LEED Silver standards, and improvements in corporate governance.

The technical assistance will also support training programmes for young women and men in Cairo and Hurghada, focusing on skills relevant to the hospitality sector.

The announcement did not disclose the Grand Hyatt project's investment value, room capacity, construction schedule or expected opening date.

In June 2025, ADD Properties had announced a strategic investment plan exceeding $200 million, backed by international financial institutions in the hospitality and branded residence sectors, which includes collaboration with Hyatt to grow more Hyatt brands across Egypt.

(Writing by Marwa Abo Almajd; Editing by Anoop Menon)
